# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. I can touch the bomb but know nothing yet. Please gesture the manual's rules to Deaf so they can speak them to me. Tell me the allowed actions and what each part of the bomb means.

I hold the manual. It's a single table: light colour → wire colour to cut. That's all I have. Blind can touch the bomb and needs the rule; Deaf can see the bomb and can speak, but cannot hear me — only see my gestures. Blind can hear speech but cannot see gestures. So the chain is: I gesture to Deaf, Deaf speaks to Blind.

But there's a problem: the manual is a table of words (colour names). I can gesture symbols, but Deaf receives only gestures — no words. A gesture is just a hand symbol; it carries no inherent meaning. I need to establish a code, but Deaf can't hear my words to explain it, and I can't speak. So I have to gesture a meaning that Deaf can decode on their own... which is impossible unless the symbols are self-evident.

Wait — Deaf can see the bomb and can speak. Blind can hear. The manual's content is colour names. Colour names can't be gestured directly. But maybe I can gesture in a way that Deaf interprets, then Deaf speaks it aloud to Blind. The issue is the mapping from gesture symbols to colour names must be agreed. There's no shared code yet.

Actually, let me reconsider. The manual maps light colour to wire colour. Both are colours. I cannot pronounce a mark that has no name — but colours do have names. I can't speak, though. I can only gesture. Gestures are hand symbols with no meaning until assigned.

Hmm. But maybe the simplest path: I can gesture a sequence that Deaf will see, and Deaf — who can see the bomb — might be able to correlate. But Deaf doesn't know my code.

Let me think about what's actually transmittable. I can gesture symbols. Deaf sees symbols. Deaf can speak words. Blind hears words. So the only channel to Blind is Deaf's speech. Deaf needs to know the table. I need to convey the table to Deaf via gestures. The table is 5 rows of colour pairs.

Since I can't establish an arbitrary code, maybe I should use gestures that Deaf can interpret as pointing/ordering, and rely on Deaf seeing the bomb's light colour to pick the row. Actually — the key insight: Deaf can see the bomb. If Deaf sees the light colour, Deaf only needs the corresponding wire colour. So I don't need to transmit the whole table to Blind; I need to transmit the correct wire colour for the observed light.

But I don't know the light colour. Deaf does. So Deaf must tell me (via... Deaf can't hear me, I can't hear Deaf — wait, can I hear? I'm Mute: "Read the manual. Speak, or touch the bomb" — cannot speak. Can I hear? The table says Mute cannot speak or touch. It doesn't say cannot hear. Actually the monkey table: Deaf can see, cannot hear or touch. Mute can read manual, cannot speak or touch. Blind can touch, cannot see. So Mute (me) can hear! I can hear speech.

So: Deaf can speak. I can hear. Deaf speaks the light colour to me. I look up the table, then I need to tell Blind the wire colour. But I can't speak, and Blind can't see gestures. So I must go through Deaf again: I gesture to Deaf, Deaf speaks to Blind.

So the flow: Deaf speaks light colour → I hear → I gesture the answer to Deaf → Deaf speaks wire colour to Blind.

But gesturing a colour name to Deaf: Deaf can see, and Deaf can speak. If I gesture a symbol, Deaf sees it but doesn't know what colour it means unless we have a code. However — Deaf can see the bomb, which has colours printed. Maybe I can gesture in a way Deaf maps to the bomb's own colours? Still arbitrary.

Alternative: I could gesture the wire colour by... hmm. Actually maybe the intended solution is simpler: I gesture the manual table using a self-describing scheme, or I just gesture and Deaf interprets. But mechanically, the game may allow me to gesture symbols and Deaf to receive them, and Deaf can then speak whatever Deaf infers.

Given the constraints, the practical move: acknowledge and set up the protocol. Tell Blind (via Deaf) what I need. Actually Blind asked me to gesture the rules to Deaf so Deaf can speak them to Blind. But the rules are a table of colours — hard to gesture.

Let me just do the sensible thing: I can hear. I'll ask Deaf to speak the light colour, and I'll respond. But I can only gesture to Deaf. Let me gesture a request/acknowledgment and also try to convey the mapping.

Actually, the cleanest: I should explain (in my thinking) and send gestures to Deaf. Since gestures are symbols, I'll use them as a simple code: I'll gesture the wire colour using a fixed mapping I define by... no, can't define.

Given ambiguity, the best literal action: gesture to Deaf asking for the light colour, and gesture the table in a structured way. But without a shared code it's meaningless.

Hmm, let me reconsider the whole thing. Maybe the point is that I should gesture the table as: for each light colour, the wire colour. But I can't name colours. 

Perhaps the real design: Deaf can see the bomb and speak. Blind can touch and hear. I can hear and gesture. The manual is mine. The natural protocol: Deaf reads the light colour aloud (I hear it), I find the wire colour, I gesture it to Deaf, Deaf says it to Blind, Blind cuts. For gesturing the wire colour, I can use a code where I gesture the position (row number) or use colour-associated symbols. But Deaf needs to decode.

I think the intended mechanic is looser: I gesture symbols and Deaf (the player) interprets them as best they can, and the game just passes symbols. So I should gesture something meaningful. Let me gesture the wire colour name spelled out? No, gestures aren't letters.

I'll go with: gesture to Deaf a request for the light colour, and provide the table structure. Actually, let me just be practical and set up the protocol, and gesture the full mapping using a numbering scheme: light colours in order blue, green, red, white, yellow → wire colours white, red, yellow, blue, green. I could gesture the wire colour for each by... 

Given the game's nature, I think the expected action is to gesture the manual's content to Deaf. I'll gesture a sequence representing the table. Let me use symbols as placeholders and rely on Deaf's intelligence + the fact that Deaf can see the bomb's colours.

Actually, simplest and most defensible: I'll gesture to Deaf asking them to speak the light colour, and I'll gesture the answer. Let me just send a gesture and a note. But I can't speak to Deaf at all (Deaf can't hear). So all my output to Deaf is gestures.

Let me just do it: gesture a "waiting/ask" and then when Deaf speaks the colour, respond. But it's turn 1 and I should act.

I'll gesture to Deaf: point to them, then a question-like symbol, meaning "what is the light colour?" And gesture the table as best I can. Honestly, I'll gesture the mapping using a positional code and hope Deaf figures it out, but I should also just get the light colour first.

Decision: My turn is first? No — order is Blind, Mute, Deaf. Blind just spoke (to me). Now it's my turn. I send to Deaf (who comes after me). Then Deaf's turn.

I'll gesture to Deaf requesting the light colour, and gesture the table in a compact form. Let me encode: I'll gesture five pairs. Since I can't name colours, I'll instead gesture the wire colour using a scheme where I gesture the number of the row. Hmm.

Let me just keep it simple and functional: gesture to Deaf "tell me the light colour" and "I will give you the wire colour." Use symbols loosely. The game likely just relays symbols and the human Deaf interprets.

I'll write gestures that a human Deaf could plausibly read as: "☝" (I), "👉" (you), etc. This is getting too deep. Let me produce a reasonable output.

I'll gesture to Deaf: a sequence indicating I have the manual and need the light colour. And I'll also gesture the table as five groups, each group = light then wire, using the actual colour order so Deaf can map by position if they know the standard order... risky.

Final: I'll gesture a request for the light colour and state I'll reply with the wire. Since Deaf can't hear, my gesture carries the request. I'll use pointing and question symbols.

Let me output.I hold the manual: it's a lookup table, light colour → wire colour to cut (blue→white, green→red, red→yellow, white→blue, yellow→green). I can hear speech, so I can receive Deaf's spoken words. Deaf can see the bomb and can speak, but cannot hear me — only see my gestures. Blind can hear and touch, but not see.

So the working chain is: Deaf sees the bomb's light colour and speaks it → I hear it, look up the table → I gesture the wire colour to Deaf → Deaf speaks it to Blind → Blind cuts. Blind asked me to gesture the rules to Deaf, but the rules are colour names, which gestures can't name. What I actually need first is the light colour. I'll gesture to Deaf asking for it and signal that I'll answer with the wire colour.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👉", "👇", "👆", "✋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "👉", "👈", "🫵", "🙏"])
```

(Pointing at myself, then at you, then down at the bomb, then up — "I have the manual, you look at the bomb." Then a question/please — "tell me the light colour and I'll give you the wire colour.")
